$comment: Gemfall beat 5 on the River Road (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 5A). `allies` is set exactly once, by the three choices of scene_who_to_tell, which every path to every ending passes through once (it sits before the crossing and nothing loops back). `cult` is optional and only ever set by scene_cult_pitch, on one of two choices, so no path sets both. The setback needs a failed span crossing, then a failed wolf check or the fight picked, and the fight lost. The expansion's spine episodes (brass south, tremor, Nim's pony, old marks, survey guard, crack string, stones vote, span question, pack crossing, rim lookout) set only chapter-local flags; allies is still set only in scene_who_to_tell.
title: The Broken Bridge

plate.narration: A crack runs through the Northern River Bridge. A griffin engineer crouches beside it with chalk and a clipboard. Beyond the barriers, travelers wait to cross. The stones need a careful look before the road can carry on.

objectives.label: Helped somebody whose rush was over
Plotted the outline of the truth yourselves

goal.text: Cross the cracked bridge, and find out what its cracks are saying.

steps.label: Get down to the bridge foot

facet_clerks.name: The Clerk's Stone
facet_clerks.text: Logged, tagged 4117, and crossing westbound. Then, very irregularly, not.

scene_bridge.narration: Your job tonight: cross the cracked Northern River Bridge, and find out what its cracks are saying. Skywardens in silver and violet let a few travelers over at a time. The bridge looks like a plate glued back together in a hurry.

scene_spans_from_above.narration: From the air, the crack is really dozens of cracks. They all lean toward the mountain, like grass in a wind. A warden engineer looks up at you and writes something down.

scene_soup_line.narration: The soup woman's name is Hollis. DEEP HOLLOW is stitched on her apron. She hands a muddy prospector a bowl. "Eat first, dear. Questions later." His wheelbarrow has lost a wheel.

scene_soup_line_fix_barrow.narration: You knock the wheel back on with a rock. The prospector gives you his luck pebble, the only thing he has left. It is not a gem. "Worked anyway," he says.

scene_cult_pitch.narration: Hollis talks while she ladles. "The world's rules are broken, love. The power under the mountain could write new ones. The seal on it isn't a lock. It's a lid on the cure." She nods at a jar labeled THE BREAK, half full of humming stones.

scene_cult_pitch_finish_soup.narration: Hollis refills your bowl without asking. You never answer her. Behind her, the jar hums. You can still hear it at the bridge foot.

scene_cult_pitch_drop_stone.narration: You drop a coin in the jar. The humming stones buzz louder, like a hive waking up. Hollis writes your names in a little book and gives you a second bowl. You are not sure how you feel about it.

scene_cult_pitch_say_no_kindly.narration: "No, thank you," you say. Hollis keeps ladling. "That's all right, love. Soup's still free." She means it. That part stays with you all the way to the bridge.

scene_clerk.narration: At the clerk's table, a warden named Pellam logs every gem that crosses and keeps none. "Logged is not owned," he says. The tired carter brings gem 4117. Its hum makes his pen jump off the page.

check_carter.prompt: Talk a tired carter into trading gem 4117

onSuccess.narration: She has been listening to that gem hum for nine days. "Take it," she says. "Give me a song I can sing over it instead." You give her the best one you know.

onFailure.narration: "Promised to a buyer in the foothills," she says, and clicks to her mule. Gem 4117 hums away west across the bridge.

check_ledger.prompt: Find the rule that lets a logged gem change hands

onSuccess.narration: Page four hundred and twelve: a logged gem may be transferred at the crossing if both parties sign and the clerk is not on his lunch. Pellam checks his watch. He is not on his lunch.

onFailure.narration: You find a rule about goats, a rule about very large goats, and a rule about goats that are actually two children in a coat. By the time you look up, gem 4117 is across.

scene_clerk_stone.narration: Pellam crosses out WESTBOUND, writes EASTBOUND, crosses that out, and writes WITH THEM. "Very irregular," he says. "Entirely legal." The stone is cool and heavy. Its hum makes your teeth fizz.

scene_engineers.narration: Inside, Engineer Brask pins every crack in red on a chalk survey. She has a pencil behind each ear and a third lost in her hair. "Seen anything odd on the road?" she asks. "I need it. This drawing makes no sense."

check_outline.prompt: Plot everything you've seen since Bramblewood against the cracks

onSuccess.narration: You draw it in chalk: the old note the troll's bridge hums, the bent pride roads, the spiraling sashes. Then you draw the cracks over the top.

onFailure.narration: Your map comes out looking like a cat walked across it. Brask takes the chalk, says "no, no, you're right, look," and draws it again properly.

scene_outline.narration: Everything points the same way. The troll's old note, the bent pride roads, the sashes, the cracks: all of it bends around the stones, and all of it is older than the mountain's name. The stones were here first. The land has been keeping a record all along. Brask sits down on a bucket.

rest_tent.narration: The engineers share strong tea. Every cup ripples. "Even the tea is nervous," says Brask. Rest, and decide who should hear what you found.

scene_who_to_tell.narration: "Tell the wardens," says Brask, "and we can use this to run the crossing." Or Nim can ring it north to the gathering towns. Or you can keep it close until you know more. Who should hear it first?

scene_told_wardens.narration: Brask writes it all down and underlines the mountain three times. "This changes the arithmetic." She gives you a crossing pass. She has underlined that too.

scene_told_gatherers.narration: Nim listens, rings her bell once, and turns Pepper north. "Grandmother will say she told everyone." For once, Pepper does not argue.

scene_kept_close.narration: You fold your copy of the survey into your safest pocket. Brask keeps her numbers, but the whole story travels with you. Nobody else hears it today.

scene_crossing.narration: The cracked span sways under the last cart. The warden waits with her flag. Below, the river roars. Use what you prepared, show a pass if you have one, or take a plain ration turn.

check_span.prompt: Cross the swaying span before the warden's flag drops

onSuccess.narration: Step, sway, step, sway, and you're over. The warden at the far end gives you a very small nod, which from a Skywarden is practically a hug.

onFailure.narration: Halfway across, the bridge gives a long groan and the flag slams down. "Span closed! Everybody back!" The only other way over is the old pride ford, underneath.

scene_under_bridge.narration: Under the bridge, by the old ford, the stones are warm. A pack of cinder wolves lies heaped against the pillars, a long way from home. They lift their ember eyes at the hum in your packs. They do not like it.

check_wolves.prompt: Get the pack interested in supper instead of you

onSuccess.narration: Every nose turns toward the supper. You wade the ford with your boots in your hands while a dozen ember eyes ignore you completely.

onFailure.narration: The supper is gone in four seconds. The pack looks at you as if to say: is that all?

encounter_wolves.narration: The pack spreads across the shallow ford, guarding the warm side.

onVictory.narration: The wolves give way, grumbling, and pile back against their pillar. You wade across while they pretend they meant to move.

onDefeat.narration: The pack holds the ford. You end up back on the south bank, soggy and outnumbered.

scene_griffin_shortcut.narration: One at a time, you carry everybody over the gap, wings beating hard. Behind you, Pellam sighs and writes UNRATIFIED in very large letters.

scene_far_rim.narration: Past the bridge, grass gives way to red stones. The foothills of Mount Red Sky glow ahead. You climb toward the rim, with the outline of the truth in your packs.

rest_end.narration: You camp on the rim. Below, the foothills glitter with thousands of campfires: all the rush in the world. Above them, the mountain glows. Tomorrow, at Redspire, the wardens' citadel, somebody will put it all on one table.

variants.text: Your work at the crack got you across the bridge.

rest_setback.narration: Nobody is hurt. The wolves just wanted the warm side more. You wait two days on the south bank while the rush gets ahead. At last Pellam waves you across himself. "Logged," he says. "Late. But logged."

variants.text: Your work at the crack got you across the bridge.

scene_brass_south.narration: Six tired people in dented brass hats push an empty wheelbarrow south. It is the Brassbuckle Expedition, and nobody is smiling. "We are just going home," says their scout.

scene_brass_south_ask_what.narration: "Full," says the tallest one. "The foothills are full. Every stone has three people on it, and a warden writing it down." He sighs. "We should have told the troll a story." Nobody believes him, not even him.

scene_brass_south_share_supper.narration: You share your supper on the empty barrow. Then the smallest one gives you a folded paper. "Our map of the span. Keep to the east rail. It sways least. We were going to sell it."

scene_brass_south_ask_question.narration: "Where did you get that? And where is it going?" you ask. The Brassbuckles look into their barrow. It is empty. "Nowhere, now," says the tallest. "Home." This time he sounds like he means it.

scene_tremor.narration: The ground gives a long shudder. The ration line wobbles. Beside you, a tired carter's stack of crates starts to lean. She grabs for it too late.

check_crates.prompt: Everybody grab at the toppling crates

onSuccess.narration: You catch the top crate, then the next, then the next, and stand there holding a wobbling tower until the carter props it back. "Nine days those have been humming at me," she says, wiping her face. "Nine days. Thank you." One crate has a tag on it: 4117.

onFailure.narration: The crates topple straight past your hands and land, thump, thump, thump, in a hay cart. Nothing breaks. One of them bursts open, and it is full of socks. "Not that one," says the tired carter. "The humming ones are underneath." One tag says 4117.

scene_tremor_look_down.narration: When the shaking stops, the road is covered in hair-thin cracks. Every one leans the same way, toward the mountain. You look up at the bridge. Its cracks lean that way too.

scene_nim_pony.narration: At the bridge foot, a dragonling named Nim argues with her pony, Pepper. Nim is a bell-rider. She carries news north to the gathering towns, if Pepper will go. Pepper wants grass. "Help?" Nim asks. Her bell rings the whole time.

scene_nim_pony_hold_pony.narration: You cover Pepper's ears and lead her past the humming carts. She allows it, if you scratch her nose. "Grandmother says ponies always know first," says Nim. "She is usually right. It's very annoying."

check_pony.narration: Pepper has gone stiff-legged, staring at the humming carts. "She'll stand there till Tuesday," says Nim. "Do something nice at her."

interaction.cue: Do something calm and kind until Pepper's ears come forward.

options.label: Hum a slow tune
options.reaction: Pepper's ears swivel toward the sound.

options.label: Stroke her nose
options.reaction: Pepper leans into your palm with a sigh.

options.label: Offer a windfall apple
options.reaction: Pepper crunches it and forgets all about the carts.

stages: She sighs, and her feet unfreeze.

onSuccess.narration: Pepper sighs and walks on, as if it was her idea. "Only Grandmother can do that," says Nim. She gives you three coins. "Bell-rider's tip. Don't tell Grandmother."

onFailure.narration: Pepper sighs and walks on, as if it was her idea. "Only Grandmother can do that," says Nim. She gives you three coins. "Bell-rider's tip. Don't tell Grandmother."

scene_nim_pony_bell_greeting.narration: You bow and ring a pretend bell: high, low, high, the gathering-town way. Nim squeaks. "You're from the towns!" She tells you which grandmothers are feuding this year. It is most of them.

scene_old_marks.narration: Where the river has scrubbed the oldest stones bare, there are carved marks, worn almost smooth. The bridge was built right on top of them. "Always been there," says a passing warden. "Nobody reads them."

check_rubbing.narration: The marks only show in just the right light. The warden lifts her lantern, and the shapes glow one at a time. "Quick," she says. "Light moves." Watch them, then draw them back in order.

interaction.cue: Watch the marks glow, then draw them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: Rub, rub, rub. A spiral comes up, black and clear, curling around a little circle. Just like the sashes at the waystation. You roll it up carefully.

onFailure.narration: Rub, rub. You get a perfect picture of a warden's boot. She was standing on your paper. She asks to keep it.

onAssisted.narration: The warden holds her lantern still for you. Rub, rub, rub. A spiral comes up, curling around a little circle, just like the sashes at the waystation.

scene_old_marks_palm.narration: You lay a palm on the old stone, the way Old Lintel does. Deep down, you feel it: the same note your packs hum. This stone was humming long before the bridge, or the rush.

scene_old_marks_read_marks.narration: You see what everybody walks past. These marks have been carved again and again, for hundreds of years, to keep the spiral clear. Somebody has kept this record a very long time. You copy every line.

scene_survey_guard.narration: In the engineers' tent, they are mapping the bridge's cracks. Corporal Tibbet guards the door. He is very new, and his helmet is too big. "No entry without a pass. Or a good reason. In writing." He holds out a clipboard.

check_tibbet.prompt: Convince a very serious corporal to let you in

onSuccess.narration: You tell him about the old note the troll's bridge hums, and the bent roads, and the spiraling sashes. Tibbet listens with his mouth slightly open. Then he remembers he is a corporal, closes it, salutes, and lifts the tent flap for you.

onFailure.narration: Tibbet listens to every word, writes "REASON: LONG" on his clipboard, and says no. Then an engineer pokes her head out, says "Tibbet, let them hold the string," and pulls you around the side of the tent.

scene_survey_guard_write_it.narration: You write your reason in your best letters: WE THINK THE STONES ARE OLDER THAN THE MOUNTAIN. Tibbet reads it twice. He goes a little pale and holds the flap open.

scene_survey_guard_clerks_stone.narration: You show Tibbet the Clerk's Stone, tag 4117, marked WITH THEM in Pellam's hand. Tibbet salutes the stone. Then, to be safe, he salutes you too. "Logged goods may pass," he says.

scene_crack_string.narration: Behind the tent, two apprentices measure a crack with knotted string. One has chalk on both eyebrows. You have time for one job: hold the string to learn rope bracing, or read the chalk to learn when the span goes still.

check_string.narration: The apprentice stretches the knotted string along the crack. "Hold this end? It only reads true when it's tight. One hero reads the knots. Everyone else pulls."

interaction.cue: Friends pull the string tight while someone reads the knots.

onSuccess.narration: You hold it steady as a heron's leg. The apprentice counts the knots. "A hair wider than yesterday," she sighs. "It's always a hair wider than yesterday."

onFailure.narration: A breeze makes the string wiggle like a worm. The apprentice laughs and measures it herself. "A hair wider than yesterday. Always is."

onAssisted.narration: The apprentice props one end while you pull the line tight. With her help, you learn to brace a crossing rope.

scene_crack_string_read_chalk.narration: The chalk marks show the crack growing, cart by cart. The apprentice points to the quiet moment after each cart, when the span goes still. You copy it down. Her eyebrows drop chalk on the page.

scene_engineers_rubbing.narration: You lay your copy of the old marks beside the survey. Brask looks from one to the other. The old spiral and her new cracks curl around the very same point. She reaches for her left pencil, then her right.

choice_stones_on_table.narration: Brask looks at your packs. "Those are humming," she says. "May I see them, on the survey?" The whole tent goes quiet. Will you lay your stones on the table? Everybody vote.

choice_stones_on_table_lay_out.narration: You set your stones on the chalk drawing. They hum together like a little chord. Brask's tea starts to ripple. She moves the cup to the end of the table, then onto the floor.

choice_stones_on_table_keep_shut.narration: "Not yet," you say. Brask nods. "Fair. You carried them." She writes KEPT SHUT in the corner of the survey and underlines it. You feel proud, and a little bit watched.

choice_stones_on_table_pride_stone.narration: You set down the Pride Stone. It came from the middle of the widest bend, where no pride would set a paw. Brask writes PRIDE COUNTRY: AVOIDED BY EVERYONE and circles it. Then she circles the circle.

scene_span_question.narration: At the bridge end, the warden with the flag stops you. "Where did you get that?" she asks. "And where is it going?" It is Old Lintel's question, word for word, a whole country from his bridge.

scene_span_question_answer.narration: You tell her everything, from the Exchange docks to here. She writes it all down. "Nobody else answers properly," she says. "They just say 'mine' and 'north.'"

scene_span_question_ask_back.narration: "From a carter," she says, "who had it from a centaur, who had it from a manticore, who had it from a troll." She shrugs. "Good question. Nobody has a good answer."

scene_span_question_river_asked.narration: "The river asked us first," you say. "It carried us all the way to the sea." The warden blinks. Then she laughs, the first Skywarden laugh you have heard. "Did you have an answer?" You are still working on that.

scene_pack_crossing.narration: Packs cross the bridge apart from people. Pellam offers the wardens' gem cart, or your own arms. "Logged is not owned," he says. The cart hums like a hive. Its mule looks unimpressed.

scene_pack_crossing_carry.narration: Pellam writes CARRIED, BY HAND, BY CHOICE. You keep the packs close. He thinks about underlining it, then saves the underline for later.

scene_pack_crossing_cart.narration: Your packs ride the gem cart. The bridge groans, and every warden checks the span. On the far side, Pellam hands them back. Still logged. Still yours.

scene_pack_crossing_reed_knot.narration: You wind Old Ossley's wet reed knot around your packs. The hum goes soft, like a faraway river. Pellam writes QUIETER THAN EXPECTED. "Most irregular," he says, pleased.

check_span_quiet.prompt: Cross along the steady east rail before the flag drops

onSuccess.narration: Along the east rail the span hardly sways at all. You walk over almost easily, and the warden at the far end gives you a very small nod. The Brassbuckles' map was right. You hope somebody tells them.

onFailure.narration: The east rail is steadier, but not steady enough. Halfway over, the bridge groans and the flag slams down. "Span closed! Everybody back!" The only other way over is the old pride ford, underneath.

scene_rim_lookout.narration: A new centaur marker reads REDSPIRE, ONE DAY. Bracken Swiftmile, a relay centaur, skids up, her sash stuffed with letters. "Relay waits for nobody! Anything going south?"

scene_rim_lookout_send_word.narration: You write two short letters. One for Elder Sefa: the cubs were right, the stones really sing. One for Old Lintel: we are finding out. "Troll'll take a year to read it," says Bracken, and gallops south.

check_fires.prompt: Count the rush's campfires in the foothills below

onSuccess.narration: You count in hundreds, then in patches, then in valleys. Bracken helps. Your best guess is four thousand and twelve, and Bracken writes it down to carry south. "Biggest rush in living memory," she says, and whistles. "And all of it humming."

onFailure.narration: One, two, three... you lose count at three hundred and something, when a cloud moves and a whole valley of fires appears at once. "More than stars," says Bracken, and that will have to do. She trots off south with your news.

scene_rim_lookout_fly_redspire.narration: You fly high into the red evening. On the tallest foothill stands a black citadel, shining like a wet stone: Redspire, where the wardens keep their records. You tell Bracken. She knew, but lets you tell her.

interaction_bowls.narration: Up the line, a woman with a bathtub-sized soup pot needs help. You pass bowls to the tired travelers. The carter nearly uses her hat as a bowl. Not a drop spills. The soup woman tucks a wrapped supper into your pack.

interaction_level.narration: Brask brings a tray of water with a tiny cork boat on it. "Engineers' level." Carry it flat across the planks. Keep the boat in the middle.

interaction.cue: Everyone lift or lower your side until the water is flat, then carry the tray.

onSuccess.narration: The cork boat never moves. "Level to a hair," says Brask. "The approach is sound. It's the middle that worries me."

onFailure.narration: Water slops over, and the cork boat goes for a swim. "Either the plank leans or you do," says Brask, mopping with her hat.

onAssisted.narration: Brask steadies one side, and the water lies flat. "Level to a hair. It's the middle that worries me."

scene_lantern_wisps.narration: Two tiny, giggling wisps have untied the lantern strings on the gem cart. The lamps swing wild. The mule starts to complain. "Get them off before the whole line spooks!" shouts Brask.

encounter_wisps.narration: The wisps zip around the cart, tugging strings and giggling. Drive them off before the mule bolts.

scene_wisps_shooed.narration: The wisps bob away over the river, still giggling. Brask scoops their leftover glow into a jar. "Free light," she says. "Take it. The tent has plenty."

scene_wisps_scattered.narration: The wisps swirl the bridge into dizzy sparkles. Brask bangs a pot lid on the rail, and they pop away like soap bubbles. No jar of glow tonight, but the mule is calm.

scene_rim_lookout_pay.narration: You press a coin into Bracken's hand. Your letters go in the front of her sash. "Priority post!" She gallops south, and one very old letter flutters out onto your boot.

interaction_crossing_signal.narration: She shows you the signals: wait, walk, wait. The river is too loud for shouting. Repeat the flags in order.

interaction.cue: Watch the signals, then repeat them in order.

interaction_flag_rope.narration: The warden with the flag ties her loose signal rope back up. She waves you to the rail. "Learn my flags before your turn."

interaction_transfer_rule.narration: Pellam opens the transfer page. The carter agrees to give you the humming gem in return for a song she can sing over it. Put the steps in order before she signs. Pellam has a fresh pen. He is keeping it firmly on the page.

interaction.cue: Share the rule clues and prepare the agreed transfer.
clues: Match the gem tag before anyone signs.
The carter and the new carriers both sign after the tag is checked.
Record the new destination after both signatures.

onSuccess.narration: Tag checked, both signatures made, new destination recorded. You sing for the carter. Pellam approves the transfer.

onFailure.narration: You find a rule about goats, a rule about very large goats, and a rule about goats that are actually two children in a coat. By the time you look up, gem 4117 is across.

onAssisted.narration: Pellam points to each step while you check it. The carter signs, you sing, and the agreed transfer is recorded with help.

interaction_survey_evidence.narration: Lay what you noticed beside the survey. Everybody adds a piece: a road you walked, something near the stones, or one of Brask's numbers. Brask moves her tea out of the way first.

interaction_survey_line.narration: The warden has checked the crossing rope. Hold it tight, the way you practiced, while one hero guides the crossing. Alone, use the fixed post.

interaction.cue: Brace the checked rope while the acting hero guides the crossing.

onSuccess.narration: The brace holds steady. The warden guides you over the checked span.

onFailure.narration: The rope goes slack. The warden closes the span and leads you down to the old ford.

onAssisted.narration: The warden braces the post beside you. Together you keep the rope tight and cross.

interaction_settled_span.narration: The last cart clears the span. Your notes show the quiet moment. Wait for the warden's gold signal, then step out.

interaction.cue: Step when the gold signal marks the settled interval.

onSuccess.narration: You step out in the quiet moment. The warden holds the carts until you are across.

onFailure.narration: You stop when the flag drops. The span needs checking again, so the warden sends you to the old ford.

onAssisted.narration: The warden calls the quiet moment from your notes. With her help, you cross before the carts move.

interaction_survey_evidence_response_roa.narration: Your road goes beside the crack lines. Brask checks where it bends. Your road and her cracks curve the same way.

interaction_survey_evidence_response_sto.narration: Brask marks the places you describe, asking where the observation came from. Your clues and her cracks curve the same way.

interaction_survey_evidence_response_mea.narration: Brask reads yesterday and today from the survey. One pencil falls out of her hair. Her numbers and your clues curve the same way.

voiceGuide.tone: busy, gray-coated, a bit solemn, with warm people in it; the moment the party sees the whole shape of the clue
forbidden: the cult as villains; they are kind first, always
naming what the titan or the Hollow Gate is

npcVoices.hollis: a Deep Hollow Cult recruiter with a giant soup pot; gentle, patient, calls everyone 'love'; feeds people before she says anything; sincerely believes the seal is a lid on a cure
npcVoices.pellam: a Skywarden clerk; dry, precise, logs everything and keeps nothing; 'logged is not owned'; secretly enjoys irregular-but-legal
npcVoices.brask: Skywarden engineer; pencils behind both ears; blunt and honest; talks about arithmetic and acceptable losses but is not unkind
npcVoices.carter: a tired caravan driver; has heard gem 4117 hum for nine days; trades for a song; grateful when you catch her crates
npcVoices.nim: a dragonling bell-rider on a tiny fast pony called Pepper; quick, proud, a little sassy about her grandmother
npcVoices.brassbuckles: the Brassbuckle Expedition, coming home south with an empty wheelbarrow and dented hats; tired, honest for once
npcVoices.tibbet: Corporal Tibbet, a very new Skywarden guarding the engineers' tent; helmet too big; wants reasons in writing
npcVoices.apprentice: an apprentice engineer measuring the crack with knotted string every evening; 'a hair wider than yesterday'
npcVoices.flag_warden: the Skywarden with the flag at the span; asks the troll's question of every cart
npcVoices.bracken_swiftmile: a relay-running centaur stuffed with letters; quick, cheerful; 'relay waits for nobody, but it does catch up'

interaction_bowls.narration: Hot soup bowls come down the shaky line. Pass them hand to hand to the tired travelers. The carter takes off her hat, considers using it as a bowl, and thinks better of it.

interaction.cue: Catch the bowl, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: Not a drop spills. The last bowl reaches the tired carter, who drinks it with both hands. "Humming gives me the shakes," she says. The woman with the ladle nods at you, as if you had passed a test she never said she was giving, and tucks a wrapped supper into your pack.

onFailure.narration: One bowl slips, and a prospector catches it on his hat. "Hot hat," he says, bravely. The line laughs, and the soup goes on.

onAssisted.narration: Together you and the carter pass the bowls in a slow, steady row. Not a drop spills, and the woman with the ladle tucks a wrapped supper into your pack.

interaction_flag_rope.narration: The warden gives the signal rope a tug. Its loose end swings out over the bridge rail. Catch it as it swings back, so the flags can keep guiding the carts across.

interaction.cue: Catch the rope when it swings back to the rail.

interaction_survey_evidence.narration: Put what you noticed beside the crack survey. Say one observation aloud, or ask Brask to read one of her measurements. Each hero adds a piece. Brask moves her tea before the chalk arrives. Experience has taught her this.

interaction.cue: Each hero contributes an observation or checks a measurement.

options.label: Describe a road we walked
options.reaction: Your road goes beside the crack lines. Brask checks where it bends.

options.label: Describe what we noticed near stones
options.reaction: Brask marks the places you describe, asking where the observation came from.

options.label: Ask Brask for a bridge measurement
options.reaction: Brask reads yesterday and today from the survey. One pencil falls out of her hair.

onSuccess.narration: Your observations and the engineers' measurements fit on one survey. Together you compare the bends.

onFailure.narration: Your map comes out looking like a cat walked across it. Brask takes the chalk, says "no, no, you're right, look," and draws it again properly.

onAssisted.narration: Brask reads the survey aloud while you add your observations. Together you see where the lines meet.
